text: Band of Joy is the ninth solo studio album by English rock singer Robert Plant and the first released with his new backing group, the Band of Joy. It was released on 13 September 2010 in the UK and 14 September in the US. The album is notable for the song "Monkey," originally by the band Low, which is slowed down to a grinding, spooky gothic rock tempo and mood, differing significantly from Low's version. This track is arguably the least similar to other songs on the album (except for "Satan"), which mostly feature folk rock or progressive rock styles. Although not a regular part of Plant's live performances, it has been performed on occasion. The album debuted at #5 on the Billboard 200 chart and at #3 on the UK Albums Chart. The first single released from the album was "Angel Dance." Band of Joy received positive reviews, with Metacritic assigning it an aggregate score of 80 out of 100, indicating "generally favorable reviews." Rolling Stone gave it a three-and-a-half-star rating and ranked it #8 on its list of the 30 Best Albums of 2010. Q Magazine, in its January 2011 edition, ranked Band of Joy as the second best album of 2010, noting that Plant, free from the need to imitate his 20-year-old self from Zeppelin, sings to his strengths with Miller and Griffin as key contributors, showcasing a range of styles including gentlemanly country-blues ("Cindy, I'll Marry You Some Day"), spooky lo-fi ("Silver Rider"), and charming '60s pop ("You Can't Buy My Love"). The album was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Best Americana Album and Best Solo Rock Vocal Performance for the song "Silver Rider." Robert Plant was also nominated for Best British Male Solo Artist at the Brit Awards 2011. Sales figures are based on certification alone.
